extracted.intended_audience: college mathematics instructors and faculty-development meeting facilitators (especially new instructors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning and facilitating a faculty meeting (≈50 minutes) to help instructors describe, reflect on, and learn strategies for handling difficult individual student behaviors and difficult instructor–student situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of difficulties
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish four categories of difficulties: (1) implicit, mismatched ideas of course expectations between instructor and students; (2) difficulties that arise from the nature of the interactive classroom; (3) difficulties between individual students and the administrative structure of the course; (4) highly interpersonal situations between individual students and the instructor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this taxonomy to frame discussions; the meeting focuses on category (4) idiosyncratic instructor–student situations where prescriptive advice is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge emotional & practical issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitators should be aware that discussions will involve highly emotional issues and practical matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of emotions, practical constraints, and relevant instructor/student beliefs when facilitating; create a supportive environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception of 'weed-out' courses
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that many institutions (or students' perceptions) treat elementary mathematics courses as 'weed-out' courses, leading to heightened competition and anxiety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how this perceived climate may affect classroom interactions and motivate student behavior; address it when relevant in discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students' beliefs about mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that students may believe mathematics is memorization, that all problems are solved by textbook methods, or that all problems are quick to solve—views likely different from instructors'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitators should recognize and surface these mismatches; instructors may be unaware of students' differing epistemologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication is multimodal
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals communicate in many ways and literal verbal content is only one channel of meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to tone, body language, and non-verbal cues when addressing difficult interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic and life changes affect students
rubrics_metrics.description: Changing student demographics and life circumstances (e.g., older median age, more part-time jobs, more students who are parents) affect how students engage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitators and instructors should factor in these contextual differences when interpreting student behavior and designing responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading and evaluation as central conflict source
rubrics_metrics.description: A significant amount of difficult instructor–student interaction centers on evaluation and grading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare instructors for grading-related disputes; emphasize clarity about grading rules and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructors' past as 'good students' can bias expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Many instructors were high-achieving students who implicitly understood and followed course 'rules'; they may not anticipate that some students will try to work around or reject implicit rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage reflection on implicit assumptions about how students 'should' behave or learn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences across students' academic stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Students at different career stages have differing views of material and what constitutes intellectual involvement (e.g., beginners see material as authoritative facts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modify expectations and communication strategies to match students' developmental stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instructors with a forum to describe difficult interactions, hear colleagues' experiences, receive ideas for handling situations, and reflect on personal goals for instructor–student interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize support, idea-sharing, and encouraging instructors to define acceptable student behavior and responses to unacceptable behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: Opportunity to describe difficult interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Give instructors an opportunity to describe difficult interactions they have had with students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use storytelling/sharing to surface concrete examples and emotional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: Learn about colleagues' situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow instructors to hear about situations colleagues have faced which they may face as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalize encountering difficult situations and expand the repertoire of known cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: Share strategies for handling situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an opportunity for instructors to hear others' ideas of how to deal with difficult situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect practical tactics and adapt them to local context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: Reflect on instructor priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage instructors to think about what is important to them in instructor–student interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit instructors’ values so responses align with their teaching goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: Teach techniques for assertiveness & managing confrontation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide appreciation for techniques for handling difficult people, being appropriately assertive, and managing confrontations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete communication skills handouts and practice opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: Provide forum for mutual feedback/support
rubrics_metrics.description: Give instructors a forum for hearing others' thoughts and receiving support about these issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster a non-judgmental atmosphere to encourage participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: gather institutional/departmental guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect relevant institutional or departmental guidelines on instructor–student interactions before the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute these to participants as background; they can constrain or guide feasible actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: customize 'Difficult Student Behaviors' handout
rubrics_metrics.description: Review and modify the 'Difficult Student Behaviors' handout to reflect the student body at your institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localize examples so they resonate with participants' experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: review communication & conflict handouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Review handouts on 'Strategies for Clear Communication and for Managing Confrontation' prior to the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ready to highlight key points and answer questions about these strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: circulate agenda in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Circulate the meeting agenda to all participants well in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance distribution increases participant preparation and the quality of contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: make copies and confirm attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: Make copies of meeting materials and any questionnaires you plan to distribute, and confirm attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logistics: ensure materials are available and numbers are known for planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda item: differences between individual vs class-wide difficulties
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss differences between dealing with difficult individual students and dealing with class-wide teaching situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight when it is appropriate to address individuals versus the whole class; warn against singling out individuals inappropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda item: strategies for clear communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe general strategies for clear and unambiguous communication when managing disagreements and confrontations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use handouts and examples to illustrate communication pitfalls and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda item: catalog difficult student behaviors and strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss different kinds of difficult behavior students exhibit, and strategies for dealing with each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'Potentially Difficult Instructor–Student Interactions' handout to prompt discussion and problem-solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda item: peer discussion/opportunity to speak
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide opportunities for participants to speak with other instructors about difficult student behaviors and receive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pair/share and group-report formats to surface practical solutions and provide support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting format: Formal meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: A structured format (with a detailed timetable) suitable for imparting information and strategies when participants are less comfortable sharing personal experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested schedule: intro (0–5m), clear communication handout (5–15m), managing conflict handout (15–25m), potentially difficult interactions discussion/pairing (25–45m), wrap-up (45–50m). Use experienced instructors to answer questions and illustrate points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting format: Informal get-together
rubrics_metrics.description: A loosely structured, participant-driven format suitable if the leader aims mainly to have instructors speak with each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use handouts as supplements; provide a few guiding discussion questions and optional sample agenda items to spark conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting format: Semi-formal meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: A hybrid format combining presentation of handout content with participant discussion; leader must manage time and participant priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a loose schedule and allow participants to choose which agenda items to emphasize; place broadly interesting items early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make communication absolutely clear & unambiguous
rubrics_metrics.description: When addressing student behavior, be absolutely clear and unambiguous about the issue so that the conversation can focus on the behavior rather than misunderstandings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight main points on an overhead/board; avoid vague statements; ensure participants can ask clarifying questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage using experienced instructors as resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Call on experienced instructors during the meeting to suggest answers and provide examples from their own experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experienced instructors can model responses and offer practical advice; use them actively to answer participant questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pair/share and group reporting for problem-solving
rubrics_metrics.description: Have participants pair up to describe difficult incidents and generate suggestions, then report back to the whole group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pairs can brainstorm solutions; plenary reporting spreads ideas and allows facilitator steering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrap-up: consult colleagues and document incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Advise instructors to consult trusted colleagues before irreversible actions and to document any situations immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation is important because students may complain to administrators; consulting colleagues helps avoid unwise unilateral decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide meeting materials (handouts & guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute copies of institutional guidelines, modified 'Potentially Difficult Instructor–Student Interactions', 'Techniques for Clear Communication', 'Managing Conflict', and (for semi-formal meetings) the timetable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure handouts are tailored to the local context and distributed in time for participant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize common difficult student behavior types (scenarios)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be familiar with representative scenarios: post-test agitation claiming understanding, high-achiever struggling with non-standard problems, dominant student speaking out of turn, public exit/confrontation when collecting quizzes, students disputing grades or requesting extra work/grade changes, persistent struggling student overusing office hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these scenarios to ground discussion and practice feedback strategies; customize to local examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active listening: judge content, hold fire, listen for ideas, be flexible
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish hearing from listening; adopt key listening behaviors such as judging content not delivery, holding your fire, listening for ideas, being flexible, resisting distractions, and signaling comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt the list of good/bad listener characteristics to instructor–student contexts; practice listening behaviors in role-plays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to improve listening
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve listening by caring about improvement, finding an interruption-free place, not finishing the student's sentences, paying careful attention (take notes and address misconceptions one at a time), and being aware of emotionally charged 'red-flag' words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If red-flag words appear, consider taking a break to let emotions cool before continuing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaking strategies: prepare, check understanding, manage 'motor mouth'
rubrics_metrics.description: Address speaking problems by (a) taking a break or scheduling follow-up when words fail, (b) asking for confirmation when unsure if the listener follows, and (c) using guiding questions or notes to curb over-talking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When instructors are verbose, prepare notes/outlines or rehearse; when students are verbose, use focused guiding questions to steer conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paraphrasing to confirm and clarify
rubrics_metrics.description: Use paraphrasing to express meaning in other words to confirm understanding, clarify ambiguous statements, or reveal discrepancies between what the speaker says and the intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paraphrase as a check-point during conversations to ensure shared understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback process (steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: A structured feedback process: (a) describe the problem/situation, (b) define your feelings/reactions, (c) suggest a solution or ask the student to propose one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use feedback to structure interactions and address difficult behaviors quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for giving effective feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines: (a) ensure the student is ready, (b) base comments on facts not emotions, (c) be as specific as possible, (d) give feedback soon after the event, (e) aim for privacy, (f) focus on what the student can change, (g) request the student's cooperation, (h) focus on one issue at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these to increase the likelihood of constructive outcomes; cite concrete instances rather than vague complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding conflict vs. long-term effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoiding conflict may be tempting in the short term, but short-term ease can create long-term problems (e.g., granting extra work to one student sets precedent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider long-term classroom fairness and precedent when resolving immediate confrontations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding causes of conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Three common causes of conflict: adversarial action (win-lose framing), tightly held positions (refusal to work towards shared goals), and emotional involvement (attachment to positions or methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which cause is operating to pick appropriate conflict-management strategies (e.g., reframing, fostering joint goals, reducing emotional charge).
